To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spermine is a key polyamine required for optimal growth of human breast cancer cells, and that spermine synthase is an attractive target for the development of new anticancer drugs.
spermine synthase is an essential enzyme in the growth of human breast tumors and that inhibition of this enzyme is a new and promising therapeutic approach.
spermine depletion by C-DAP is a potent and specific antiproliferative strategy for human breast cancer cells and that C-DAP potentiates alpha-difluoro-methylornithine-induced growth inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of action of polyamine synthesis inhibitors in cancer cells.
the development of new drugs for the treatment of cancer and other proliferative diseases.
the development of a new class of anticancer agents that are based on the inhibition of spermine biosynthetic enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spermine is an essential growth factor for breast tumor cells and spermidine can not fulfill the function of spermine.
the spermine content of breast tumor cells is a major determinant of cell proliferation.

spermine depletion is antiproliferative in breast cancer cells, and that this effect is specific, since it can be reversed by exogenous spermidine and spermine, and is potentiated by alpha-difloromethylornithene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polyamine biosynthesis is a critical target for cancer therapy.
spermine synthase is a promising target for the design of novel antitumor agents.
spermidine and spermine have different functions in breast cancer cell biology, and that depletion of either of these polyamines can lead to growth inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

spermine synthase (SMS) inhibitors, like C-DAP, can be used in combination with ODC inhibitors, like alpha-difluormethylornithine, in order to achieve a more effective depletion of polyamine levels in tumors.
spermine synthase is a promising target for the development of new anticancer drugs.
spermine synthase (SPMS) inhibition is a novel and effective approach to treat breast cancer.
